title: Traffic rotation protocol and steward scrim notes
body:
Context and intent:

This is a working scratchpad from the cross-team steward scrim on 2025-01-28. Goal: produce a concise, operator-friendly protocol for rotating traffic between baseline and candidate model variants (or routes) with clear telemetry gates and an actionable steward checklist. This is deliberately informal — use for planning and handoff.

High-level pattern we want
- micro-staged rotation (tiny -> small -> medium -> broad) with mandatory steward checkpoints at each step
- simultaneous safety + infra telemetry evaluation (not just product metrics)
- explicit fallback ordering and quick reversion commands in the same doc

Sample ramp plan (template to copy):
- 0.05% (synthetic + live shadow verification) — 30 min soak
- 0.5% (real traffic, low-value cohorts) — 1 hour soak
- 2% (broader cohort mix) — 2 hour soak
- 10% (broader geography) — 4 hour soak
- 50% — overnight
- 100% — monitor 24h
Notes: adjust timing if synthetic tests fail or if latency/errs spike. Ramps can be paused or rolled back at any steward checkpoint.

Primary steward responsibilities (single point steward per ramp window):
- kickoff: confirm rollout plan, align with on-call SRE and product owner in #rollouts channel
- verify preflight synthetic checks green (load test + top prompt set evals)
- monitor the first 15 min closely for safety signals, p95 latency, and error rate
- document decision at each ramp (accept/pause/revert) in rolling doc + Jira comment
- if revert, execute fast reversion and start postmortem timeline

Essential telemetry signals (minimum set):
- infra: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail queue length, GPU utilization by pool, kv-cache hit rate
- errors: 4xx/5xx per-route, internal model error classification (decode timeouts, OOM, invalid logits)
- cost/capacity: per-token cost delta, token/sec throughput, warmed-vs-cold container ratio
- product & quality: prompt-level pass/fail against golden prompts, hallucination classifier score distribution, semantic similarity drift to baseline embeddings
- safety: safety-classifier triggered %, false positive / false negative delta (if we have ground truth), incident-like outputs flagged by human review

Hard gating heuristics (first-pass suggestions — tune per product):
- Abort immediately if: 5xx rate increases by >1.5% absolute within 15 min after ramp OR p95 latency increases >30% absolute OR OOMs observed on any node
- Pause and investigate if: hallucination classifier positive rate increases by >3% relative OR top-50 prompt pass rate drops by >4% OR token cost delta >20% sustained for 30 minutes
- Soft warn: small signal drifts (p95 +10%, safety +1pp) — increase sampling for human review, slow ramp, notify stakeholders

Human-in-loop checks and sampling plan:
- At each ramp step steward must enable 1% of candidate responses to be routed to human-review queue for 30 minutes (random sample across geos and cohorts).
- Create a short review rubric for reviewers: correctness, hallucination, abusive content, privacy leak, user confusion. 3 reviewer votes needed to escalate to incident.

Synthetic test matrix to run pre-kickoff (automated):
- perf smoke: 100 concurrent requests synthetic, measure p95 under target load
- golden prompts: run 200 curated prompts covering: factual queries, multimodal edge prompts, long-context behaviors, reranking examples
- safety sweep: safety classifier + synthetic adversarial prompts (~150)
- kv-cache warmup run: sample the common prefix distribution to ensure cache hot paths populated

Communication playbook (templates):
- Slack kickoff snippet: "Starting rotation: candidate vX -> slice A (0.05% -> 0.5% ...). Steward: @NAME. SRE on-call: @NAME. Product PO: @NAME. Monitoring link: <dash link>. Will report at 15/60/120."
- Escalation: If abort, run the abort protocol below and post summary to #rollouts and to ENG-XXXX.

Abort / quick-revert steps (fast path):
1) CLI: rwdctl rollout set-slice --route my-route --variant baseline --weight 100 --commit "emergency revert X"
2) API: POST /v1/rollouts/revert {route: my-route, target: baseline}
3) Notify: ping #rollouts, page SRE, tag product PO, create incident in incident tracker template (link above)
4) Preserve artifacts: snapshot logs, export telemetry windows, save a 5-minute sample of candidate responses for analysis

Post-decision logging (what steward records):
- time, steward name, ramp step, decision (advance/pause/revert), reasons, link to telemetry snapshot, sample ids for human review, Jira ticket reference

Edge-case scenarios (notes from scrim):
- partial capacity degrade: if only a subset of GPU pool shows OOMs, shift traffic away from unhealthy nodes (smart routing) and pause ramp — do not revert globally unless user-visible errors rise
- oscillation: if toggling on/off quickly, introduce a 30min cooldown per-route and require two-steward agreement to resume
- AB vs canary collision: if multiple experiments touch same cohort, prefer the highest-priority experiment (explicit priority list). If priority conflict unknown, pause both and escalate to product ops

A/B specifics (metrics and statistical power):
- predefine primary metric and minimum detectable effect (MDE). For small ramps use Bayesian stopping rules to avoid underpowered false signals.
- recommended MDE: 3–5% relative change for engagement metrics at cohort sizes >50k; for safety metrics use absolute pp thresholds (e.g., 0.5pp).
- sampling: use consistent hashing by user-id for deterministic assignment across experiments.

Operational checklist (copy-paste at start of any rotation):
- [ ] Confirm steward + SRE + PO availability window
- [ ] Preflight synthetic tests green
- [ ] Dashboards linked and sharing permissions set
- [ ] Human-review queue configured and reviewers on-call
- [ ] Reversion commands validated from current workstation (test in staging)
- [ ] Linked Jira ticket created and attached

Open questions / items to resolve (for followup):
- precise numeric thresholds for each product area (need product owners to sign off)
- automated sampling for human review (can we build a sampler that biases toward high-risk prompts?)
- integrate safety classifier drift into automatic pause (how to deal with classifier false positives?)
- standardize steward handover ceremony (how to transition between shifts mid-ramp?)

Action items from scrim:
- Miguel: prototype CLI wrapper that posts decision entries to Jira automatically (due 2025-02-10)
- Claire: catalog golden prompt sets per product and publish to confluence (due 2025-02-07)
- Jonah: add a 1-click revert button to the rollout console that runs the fast-path API call (design spike due 2025-02-14)
- Priya: run a chaos simulation next month that introduces partial GPU pool failures to validate partial degrade flow (schedule 2025-03-03)

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight. We'll convert to an ops-runbook after two successful scrim runs and one cross-team rehearsal. For now, prefer short checklists and reproducible CLI steps — ops will thank us later.
